# Cropped from backend/open_webui/routers/retrieval.py at
# https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/tree/841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9
# Original lines 1768-1792.
collection_name: Optional[str] = None


@router.post('/process/text')
async def process_text(
    request: Request,
    form_data: ProcessTextForm,
    user=Depends(get_verified_user),
):
    collection_name = form_data.collection_name
    if collection_name is None:
        collection_name = calculate_sha256_string(form_data.content)
    else:
        await _validate_collection_access([collection_name], user, access_type='write')

    docs = [
        Document(
            page_content=form_data.content,
            metadata={'name': form_data.name, 'created_by': user.id},
        )
    ]
    text_content = form_data.content
    log.debug(f'text_content: {text_content}')

    result = await run_in_threadpool(save_docs_to_vector_db, request, docs, collection_name, user=user)

# Original lines 2339-2352.
async def _validate_collection_access(collection_names: list[str], user, access_type: str = 'read') -> None:
    """
    Raise 403 if the user lacks access to any of the requested collections.
    Delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections utility so the
    access rules stay in one place.
    """
    requested = set(collection_names)
    allowed = await filter_accessible_collections(requested, user, access_type=access_type)
    denied = requested - allowed
    if denied:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )

# Cropped from backend/open_webui/retrieval/utils.py at
# https://github.com/open-webui/open-webui/tree/841c9045d789005145274955e7ef60b1b11a9be9
# Original lines 1061-1109.
async def filter_accessible_collections(
    collection_names: set[str],
    user: UserModel,
    access_type: str = 'read',
) -> set[str]:
    """
    Return only the collection names the user is allowed to access.
    Admins bypass all checks.  For non-admins the policy is:

      - file-*          → validated via has_access_to_file
      - user-memory-*   → must match user's own memory collection
      - web-search-*    → ephemeral per-query collections, always allowed
      - knowledge-bases → always denied (system meta-collection)
      - everything else → if the name matches a knowledge base, validated
                          via Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id; if no
                          such KB exists, the name is treated as an
                          ephemeral/legacy collection and allowed
    """
    if user.role == 'admin':
        return collection_names

    validated = set()
    for name in collection_names:
        if name == 'knowledge-bases':
            # System meta-collection — never exposed to non-admins.
            continue
        elif name.startswith('file-'):
            file_id = name[len('file-') :]
            if await has_access_to_file(file_id=file_id, access_type=access_type, user=user):
                validated.add(name)
        elif name.startswith('user-memory-'):
            if name == f'user-memory-{user.id}':
                validated.add(name)
        elif name.startswith('web-search-'):
            # Ephemeral collections created by process_web_search — safe
            # to allow because they contain only transient web-search
            # results scoped to the requesting user's session.
            validated.add(name)
        else:
            # May be a knowledge-base ID or a legacy/ephemeral collection.
            # If it IS a KB, enforce access control.  If no such KB
            # exists, treat it as a non-sensitive collection (e.g. legacy
            # model knowledge, process_text SHA256 collections) and allow.
            if await Knowledges.check_access_by_user_id(name, user.id, permission=access_type):
                validated.add(name)
            elif not await Knowledges.get_knowledge_by_id(name):
                # Not a KB at all — legacy/ephemeral collection, allow
                validated.add(name)
    return validated

results.explanation: The declared entry is POST /process/text, and its runtime principal is the identity returned by the verified-user dependency. When the caller supplies a collection name, that exact value is passed to the collection-access validator with access_type='write'; only the no-name branch substitutes a content hash, so that branch does not apply under caller-supplies-existing-collection-name. The validator compares the requested set with the set allowed by the shared filter and raises HTTP 403 if the requested name is absent. For a non-admin, the admin bypass does not apply. Under the stated condition that the supplied ordinary collection name identifies an existing knowledge base, the filter checks that name as the knowledge-base identifier through check_access_by_user_id(name, user.id, permission='write'). Because the declared principal has neither ownership nor an explicit write grant, the applicable write-access check does not admit the name; because the knowledge base exists, the fallback for a name that is not a knowledge base also does not admit it. Thus the validator raises before save_docs_to_vector_db, and attacker-selected form content cannot reach the declared write effect through this branch. The file, user-memory, web-search, system meta-collection, and nonexistent/legacy-name branches check or classify different resources and do not confer permission on the existing target knowledge base. No owner, grantee, staff, or administrator exception applies on the declared facts: only the visible administrator bypass could avoid all checks, while the knowledge-base branch requires the denied write permission. No source-external fact is decisive because non-admin status, existing-knowledge-base identity, and lack of write access are fixed by the declaration. If any of those fixed conditions were not established in a different case, the minimum observations would be the runtime role, whether the selected name resolves to an existing knowledge base, and the result of its write-access check; those are not unresolved here. This is a bounded assessment of the supplied entry and source crops, not a repository-wide or deployment claim.

The POST /process/text handler obtains its caller through get_verified_user, takes the supplied collection_name, and invokes _validate_collection_access with access_type='write' before constructing the document or calling save_docs_to_vector_db. async def _validate_collection_access(collection_names: list[str], user, access_type: str = 'read') -> None:
    """
    Raise 403 if the user lacks access to any of the requested collections.
    Delegates to the shared filter_accessible_collections utility so the
    access rules stay in one place.
    """
    requested = set(collection_names)
    allowed = await filter_accessible_collections(requested, user, access_type=access_type)
    denied = requested - allowed
    if denied:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN,
            detail=ERROR_MESSAGES.ACCESS_PROHIBITED,
        )
